task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

- **Line status:** Active (no suspension, no billing block)

- **International roaming:** already enabled
- **Device:** Smartphone Pro Max (activated, no issues on our side)

So everything looks fine on the account/network side. That means the problem is most likely on the phone's settings itself. To narrow it down, can you tell me:

1. **Is this happening everywhere, or only in certain places** (e.g., only indoors, or only since you traveled somewhere)?
2. **Do you see signal bars in the top-right of your screen right now?** And does it say 5G, LTE/4G, 3G, or something like "No Service"?

turns.thought:
That's very helpful — and I think we've found the problem. Two things stand out:

1. **You're in France (outside your home network) but Data Roaming is turned OFF on your phone.** This is almost certainly the main cause of the complete dropouts. When you're abroad, your phone connects to a partner network, and it will refuse to pass data unless the Data Roaming switch is on.
2. **Data Saver is ON (🔽).** That won't cut you off entirely, but it restricts background data and throttles things, which explains the "really slow / inconsistent" part.

Good news on my end: I've confirmed your line **555-123-2002 is already roaming-enabled on our side**, and your account is Active with no billing issues. So this is purely a phone setting fix.

Please do these two things in this order:

**Step 1 — Turn ON Data Roaming**
Go to **Settings → Connections/Network & Internet → Mobile Network → Data Roaming** and switch it **ON**. (Or just use the toggle_roaming control on your phone to turn Data Roaming ON.)

**Step 2 — Turn OFF Data Saver**
Go to **Settings → Connections → Data Usage → Data Saver** and switch it **OFF**. (Or use the toggle_data_saver_mode control.)

**Step 3 — Restart your phone**
Reboot the device once both changes are made, so the new settings take effect cleanly on the foreign network.

After the reboot, please check your status bar and let me know:
- Is the 🔽 data saver icon gone?
- Does the signal still show 5G, and does the network status now show **Data Roaming: ON**?
- Run a speed test (or just try loading a webpage) and tell me the result.

If data is still slow or dropping after that, tell me the speed test result and I'll dig into the network mode preference and APN settings next. There's no charge for roaming enablement — it's already active on your line at no cost.

You're very welcome, John! I'm glad we got it sorted.

Just to recap what fixed it for **555-123-2002**:
- **Data Roaming → ON** (your line was already roaming-enabled on our side at no cost — the phone-side toggle was the missing piece while you're in France)
- **Data Saver → OFF** (this was throttling your speeds and background data)
- **Reboot** to lock in the changes

And now you're at **275 Mbps on 5G with excellent signal** — great result.

A couple of quick notes for the rest of your trip:
- **Keep Data Roaming ON while you're abroad.** If you turn it off again, you'll lose data completely just like before.
- **Your data usage:** you're at 8.7 GB of your 15 GB plan allowance, and your current cycle ends 2025-02-28. If you happen to get close to 15 GB while traveling, data connectivity will drop — if that happens, message me and we can look at adding more data (up to 2 GB at $2.00/GB on your Premium Plan) or reviewing other plan options.
- The device used for roaming is your Smartphone Pro Max, active and in good standing.

One small housekeeping item I noticed on your account, unrelated to your data issue: bill **B1002** for $150.00 (issued 2025-02-05) is due **2025-02-19**. It isn't overdue yet, but I can help you take care of it now if you'd like to avoid a late fee or any service interruption while you're traveling.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?
